clue.text: Fast beat, yet oddly broken up

parts.note: to beat someone is to lick them, in the informal sense of thrash or defeat

indicators.note: oddly says the three letters of the word yet are to be arranged in an odd, unexpected order

parts.note: something broken up is split into parts

explanation.surface: A rhythm described as fast and yet strangely fragmented, like a stuttering drumbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns YET into ETY. 'Fast' looks like it describes the beat, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American adverb meaning at great speed, very quickly.

clue.text: Lying in wait, setting a trap to catch the king

indicators.note: to catch says one piece holds another inside it, as a trap holds its prey

parts.note: setting a trap for someone is luring them
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A hunter lies low, having set a snare to trap a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skulking unseen, ready to pounce, is behaving in this furtive way.

clue.text: Small room first added as a sitting-bower?

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison
first is written 1ST, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A tiny chamber is first extended to make a garden arbour for sitting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting-bower' looks like a shady garden seat, but read it as one who bows while seated: a player of the big string instrument held between the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello player sits to play and draws a bow across the strings.

clue.text: Designers' schemes

definitions.meaning: people who design machines and structures, read without the apostrophe as a plural noun
a verb: contrives or plots something cunningly

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means people who plan machines or bridges; the verb means contrives artfully, as in arranging a result behind the scenes.

clue.text: Substance left to ferment a year and a quarter

parts.note: Y is a standard abbreviation for year
east is one of the four quarters, or cardinal points, of the compass

explanation.surface: A brewer leaves something to ferment for fifteen months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' sounds like a fraction of the year, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus added to dough or wort is the agent that causes fermentation.

clue.text: Large cigar with band removed is flawless

indicators.note: removed says a piece is taken away from the cigar's name

parts.note: a perfecto is a large thick cigar tapering at both ends
a band is a ring, and the round letter O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A big cigar, once its paper band is slipped off, is in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The band on a cigar is a real paper ring, which makes the ring-shaped O feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any fault or defect is ideal and complete.

clue.text: I am above discrimination against pensioners in poetry-school

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first piece over the second

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
agism, also spelt ageism, is prejudice against older people

explanation.surface: Someone declares they rise above prejudice against the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century movement of poets, including Pound, favouring precise images and free verse.

clue.text: A late idea when Descartes come to life?

definitions.text: A late idea when Descartes come to life?

parts.words: A late idea when Descartes come to life?
parts.note: Descartes said 'I think, therefore I am', so his being alive came after the thinking; also a plain term for an idea that occurs later

explanation.surface: A belated notion about the philosopher Descartes springing into existence.
explanation.walkthrough: Descartes' dictum puts thinking before existing, so his life arrived only after his thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Something considered or added later, once the main thinking is over.

clue.text: Foxhunter's front runner?

parts.note: front runner looks like a leading horse or rider in the hunt, but read literally it is a limb at the front used for running, and a fox has such limbs

explanation.surface: The leading horse or rider in a fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxhunter' suggests the human riders, but it is the animal itself, or the hound, whose front limb does the running.
explanation.definitionFit: The front limb of a four-legged animal, which it runs on.

clue.text: Something outstanding to cultivate in classic art

indicators.note: in places one word within the letters of another

parts.note: ars is the classical Latin word for art
to rear plants or animals is to cultivate or raise them

explanation.surface: A notable task: growing something within the classical arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; here it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Debts that remain unpaid are said to be outstanding, still owed.

clue.text: Make medicine more acceptable — it shall purge disorder

indicators.note: disorder tells you the twelve letters of it shall purge are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A doctor promises that a laxative will cure a stomach upset, and wants to make it palatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like the illness being purged; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sweetening something unpleasant so it is easier to take, literally coating a tablet.

clue.text: On dit, that is foreign version

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters are made strange and rearranged

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A French phrase, on dit, meaning hearsay, appears as an overseas variant.
explanation.walkthrough: On dit is French for 'they say' (rumour), so 'foreign' seems to describe the phrase, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular issue or form of a book or publication is one variant of it.

clue.text: Bucketing down and overflowing

definitions.meaning: raining very heavily, a British idiom
crowded or abundantly full, as a pond full of fish

explanation.surface: Rain pours down and the gutters spill over.
explanation.definitionFit: Of rain, pouring heavily; of a place, swarming or crammed full of something.

clue.text: In one's cups there is proof

definitions.meaning: resistant to leaks, as in waterproof or airtight

explanation.surface: A drunkard insists there is evidence for his claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for drunk; also sealed so nothing gets through, as in watertight.

clue.text: Team's role, possibly, in making plastic like rubber

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be put in another arrangement

parts.note: the word team plus its S, used as letters

explanation.surface: A team's contribution, perhaps, to manufacturing a rubbery plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of Team's counts as a letter in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymer that stretches and returns to shape, such as synthetic rubber.

clue.text: What tourists in Greece see — storage tower put up to carry a harvest

parts.note: a harvest is a crop, and the tower carries 'a crop' perched above it in this down entry

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: Sightseers in Greece watch a grain silo being raised to hold the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the tower, and in this down entry it stands beneath the harvest, carrying it. 'storage tower' suggests something modern, far from ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient hilltop citadel of Athens, crowned by the Parthenon, is a major sight for visitors.

clue.text: Work-force down? Alternative is an autocrat!

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to press is to force something downwards
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Is the labour force depressed? A dictator might be the other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work-force' reads as one word, the staff, but it splits into work and force down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules harshly and crushes those beneath him.

clue.text: Parking in road, perhaps, they exploit immigrant workers

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: perhaps says in road might be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Parking in the road, they take advantage of migrant labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for bosses or employers, especially exploitative ones of immigrant labour in America.

clue.text: Booted out, disconsolate without a leader?

indicators.note: without a leader says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: disconsolate means dejected, downcast

explanation.surface: Thrown out, and feeling miserable without anyone to lead them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrown out or expelled forcibly from a place.

clue.text: Test pair?

definitions.meaning: a Test is an international cricket fixture
a pair of things that go together

explanation.surface: Is this a test of a couple?
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket Test is a type of sporting contest; also two things that correspond, a well-suited couple.

clue.text: Wonder where vehicle overturned in race?

indicators.note: in places one word within the letters of another

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race

indicators.note: overturned, in a down clue, says the word is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An amazing escape when a car flips over during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses the vehicle. 'Wonder' looks like a verb asking a question; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An extraordinary, inexplicable event is something marvellous.

clue.text: Can knot ties in less than minute

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: to knot ties is to twist them, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Can anyone tie a knot in less than a minute?
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' turns TIES into IEST. 'minute' is the adjective, very small, not sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallest of all, so even smaller than the merely very small.

clue.text: Devices used in Globe's first staged production

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Globe's
a production stages things anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stage machinery used in the opening production at the Globe theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is Shakespeare's London theatre, so a staged production feels natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mechanical contraptions or tools are clever appliances.

clue.text: Lorelei said to be farther north

parts.note: farther spoken sounds like father, and a father is a sire

explanation.surface: The Rhine maiden is said to live further north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' works on 'farther' only, making father, whose synonym SIRE is used; N then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei of German legend is a Rhine maiden who lures sailors to their doom with song.

clue.text: Edible root in mean crop

parts.note: par is the average or normal level
to snip is to cut or crop

explanation.surface: A vegetable root found in a poor harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' and 'crop' look like an adjective and noun; they are a noun meaning average and a verb meaning cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale tapering root vegetable eaten cooked, related to the carrot.

clue.text: Horse harnessed for revolutionary and better half?

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a revolutionary

indicators.note: half takes the back three letters of better

explanation.surface: A horse in harness for a revolutionary and his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse; it is the back half of the word better.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred and trained for harness racing at a trotting gait.

clue.text: Go without duck, say, but like milk

indicators.note: say tells you the words are spoken and heard as a single word

parts.note: to go without is to lack, and the teal is a small duck: lack teal

explanation.surface: Someone forgoes duck but has something milky instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or resembling milk, a scientific adjective.

clue.text: Last disposable wrapper in a box?

definitions.text: Last disposable wrapper in a box?

parts.words: Last disposable wrapper in a box?
parts.note: the final cloth a body is wound in before going into a coffin, the box

explanation.surface: Packaging thrown away at the end, wrapped inside a carton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' suggests a parcel; it is a coffin, and 'Last' means the final one a person wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A shroud: the cloth wrapped round a corpse for burial.
